summary.text: James Pericola is the Democratic nominee for the open Florida 11th Congressional District seat.

An attorney raised in Central Florida, he began as a staffer for Sen. Bob Graham, served in the Clinton administration and later worked as a government affairs executive, according to his campaign website.
He says he moved home to care for his aging mother and is running on lowering costs, protecting Social Security, Medicare and healthcare, and democracy issues.

paragraphs.text: Pericola says he was raised in Central Florida in a working-class family and is the first in his family to attend college and law school; he graduated from Spruce Creek High School.
He earned a bachelor's degree in 1997 and a law degree in 2005 from the Catholic University of America.

Pericola began his career working for U.S. Sen. Bob Graham of Florida as a special assistant, traveling the state with him, according to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; his campaign website describes the role as staff assistant.
He served in the Clinton administration as a presidential appointee, Special Assistant to the Chairman of the National Transportation Safety Board, according to his campaign website.

He describes more than 30 years in public service as a congressional staff member, attorney and senior government affairs executive who advised companies, local governments, labor organizations, trade associations and nonprofits.
Pericola says he moved home to Central Florida to care for his aging mother, an experience he cites as shaping his focus on healthcare costs.
He won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary for Florida's 11th District with 46.3% of the vote, defeating Royal Webster and Dan Williams.
According to his campaign website, he is a husband and father.
